script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

EXT. SMALL TOWN - DAY

A picturesque AMERICAN TOWN nestled in the rolling hills. The sun casts golden rays over the quaint houses and well-manicured lawns. A group of PEOPLE of all ages and walks of life gather at the edge of TOWN SQUARE.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
In this small town, there's one thing that unites everyone: the love for sports.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - DAY

Coach JAMES (50s, stern but fair) gathers his TEAM of HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS. Basketball season is upon them, and they need to shape up if they want to make it to the state championships.

COACH JAMES
We've got three weeks until the first game. I want you all in the gym every day, practicing, conditioning, and perfecting your skills.

INT. JASON'S HOME - NIGHT

JASON (16, shy, introverted), a team member, enters his dimly lit living room. He sits down on a worn-out couch, staring at an old basketball trophy on the shelf.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
But for Jason, things aren't as simple as just showing up to practice.

EXT. SMALL TOWN - DAY

Jason rides his bike through the town, passing by the local diner and the library. He stops at the mailbox, retrieving a letter. With a heavy heart, he reads the words "Eviction Notice."

INT. HIGH SCHOOL - DAY

The next day at school, Jason's friends, KIM (17, outgoing, confident) and MIKE (17, charismatic, friendly), notice something is off. They confront him, and he tells them about the eviction.

KIM
What about your family? Can't they help?

JASON
Mom lost her job last month, and Dad's been out of work for years. We've been living off savings, but it's running out.

MIKE
What about Coach James? Maybe he can help.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - NIGHT

Jason approaches Coach James after practice, explaining his situation. Coach James listens intently, then makes a decision.

COACH JAMES
I'll speak with the school board about providing you and your family with housing. In the meantime, I want you to focus on the team.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL CAFETERIA - DAY

The team gathers around Jason, showing their support. They share stories of their own struggles and how sports have helped them through tough times.

MIKE
We've got your back, man. We'll make it to the state championships for you.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL - DAY

As the days pass, Jason's teammates rally behind him, their bond growing stronger. They train hard, and their dedication pays off. They make it to the state championships, where they face a tough rival team.

EXT. STATE CHAMPIONSHIPS - DAY

The tension is high as the two teams face off on the court. Jason scores the winning basket, securing their victory and saving their small town's pride.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - NIGHT

Coach James leads his team in a celebratory huddle. He looks over at Jason, proud of his team's resilience and determination.

COACH JAMES
You all made it to the state championships, not just because of your skills, but because of who you are.

FADE OUT.

---

This modern screenplay focuses on the theme of small-town life and the unity that sports brings to a community. It tells the story of a high school basketball team and their dedicated player, Jason, who faces eviction but manages to overcome his struggles with the support of his teammates and coach. The screenplay is devoid of guns or violence and features 10-15 scenes in proper screenplay format.
